RT946x: Make mt6370_led_set_color accept composite colors Currently, mt6370_led_set_color can handle only simple colors. That is, if a green LED is turned on, other LEDs are forced to be off. To allow composit colors (e.g. red+green), this change makes mt6370_led_set_color control LEDs independently. For example, to mix green and red, it can be called as mt6370_led_set_color(LED_MASK_GREEN | LED_MASK_RED); This is consistent with other RT946x LED APIs in the sense that they also control each LED independently. ec3po_interface.py: Suppress EPIPE when writing to shutdown pipes. EC3PO uses pipes to ask the console and interpreter threads to shutdown. Those threads could potentially exit first, even just from SIGINT / KeyboardInterrupt, and in most such scenarios they will close() the read side of the shutdown pipes. BUG=b:79684405,chromium:925243 TEST=No tracebacks, hangs, or logged errors when shutting down with Servo v4 (CCD), Servo Micro, and Servo v4 + Servo Micro. I tested use of (ec|servo_(v4|micro))_uart_pty with each, and tested telling servod to quit via SIGINT (ctrl+c) and SIGTERM with each. I also edited ec3po/console.py (not in this patch) to close shutdown_pipe early in order to forcibly reproduce the crbug:925243 problem. With that change and without this patch, the same traceback occurred upon SIGINT, and servod hung until receiving another signal. With this patch, servod shut down cleanly, both from SIGINT and SIGTERM. Change-Id: I52834f8594a7013586cf2027f663b8297520ffd9 Signed-off-by: Matthew Blecker <matthewb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1450513 Reviewed-by: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@chromium.org>

init: chromeos_startup: make clobbering a little more robust If you start a dev<->verified mode transition and reboot in the middle, the next power up will trigger a powerwash which can be confusing to users. This is because we [re]use the RESET_FILE to pass args to the clobber function, and those files don't get wiped until the stateful clobbering finishes. Instead, lets use normal shell variables to hold things. This shouldn't impact system security as the other nvram settings/stateful files will still handle the transition correctly if a reboot happens. cros_generate_update_payload: Use new paygen library This is where things getting interesting. Basically this patch starts calling the chromite's paygen library instead of directly calling delta_generator. This makes everything much cleaner and extensible. Added these flags: --check: Verifies the integrity of the payload. --work_dir: This was mistakenly removed in the past. Added it back. Removed a lot of unused and unnecessary flags. Also changed the partition_lib API a bit to accommodate for optionally truncating the root partition. With this change the run time of cros_generate_update_payload increases by about 20~30 seconds. The reason being is an added extra copy that happens either from the cache to a temporary tgt_image.bin file. It might not be a good idea to get rid of that extra copy because if the file changes in the middle, the paygen can get screwed up. So we might better be safe than sorry!! I think the value we gain from this change from software engineering POV is much higher than the slight loss in the performance. We could potentially improve this by smarter caching logic in the future. BUG=chromium:862679 TEST=cros flash inside and outside chroot TEST=unittests TEST=payload-tryjob Change-Id: I66a02df093ffb65f2797904572c6b87fb76d782d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1369108 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Don Garrett <dgarrett@chromium.org>
